consumers: Rust codepet-core::agent (WP2) and the generated petstate.js via test_state_machine.mjs / test_bar_model.mjs (WP6); replayed by docs/v0.3/contracts/check_contracts.py

clients.name: Claude Code
clients.transport: shell command via Claude plugin hooks.json

clients.name: Hermes
clients.transport: argv spawn from the Hermes plugin

rules: argv client id is authoritative; the payload only passes a per-client schema sanity check
only top-level keys are read (depth 1); nested values are skipped unbuffered
id fields: strings <= 128 bytes of [A-Za-z0-9._:-], else the event is dropped
agent_id / subagentType present -> dropped before any write
unmapped event names or notification types -> dropped
Grok: prefer hook_event_name (PascalCase) over hookEventName (snake_case); camelCase ids

grok-cli.Stop: reason end_turn -> turn_done; channel_closed/shutdown -> session_end; other -> dropped

opencode.(synthesized): event field is one of the nine kinds

hermes.(synthesized): event field is one of the nine kinds

event_ids.formula: dig = hex(sha256(bytes read))[..16]; event_id = hex(sha256('codepet-ev1|' + client + '|' + kind + '|' + session + '|' + dig + '|' + floor(at_ms / 3000)))[..32]
notes: cases 1 and 2 share a 3 s bucket and dedupe; case 3 is the next bucket and does not

interactivity.policy: positive headless evidence -> non-interactive; no evidence or /proc unreadable -> interactive

rules.claude-code: CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT starts with 'sdk' -> false; else if the variable is absent, the nearest ancestor (depth <= 4) whose comm is 'claude' has an argv token exactly '-p' or '--print' -> false; else true
rules.codex: nearest 'codex' ancestor (depth <= 4): argv[1] == 'e', or any argv token exactly 'exec' or 'review' -> false
rules.opencode: the plugin's process.argv has the exact token 'run' or 'serve' after the binary -> false (sent as payload 'interactive')
rules.grok-cli: session-mode field once WP7 confirms it; until then the nearest 'grok' ancestor (depth <= 4) has an exact token in headless_flags, a token starting with one of headless_prefixes, or the adjacent pair 'agent' 'headless' -> false. 'agent stdio' (IDE/ACP), 'agent serve' and 'agent leader' stay interactive
rules.hermes: platform (remembered per session_id) not in hermes_platforms -> dropped by the plugin, never sent; background-review agents per WP7

interactivity.grok_source: grok 1.0.52 (0920c8169e27) `grok --help` and `grok agent --help`, read 2026-10-16 under a throwaway HOME

turn_qualifies.rule: matching turn was open AND (tools >= 1 OR duration_ms >= min_turn_ms) AND interactive AND NOT test

caps.rule: jar_full if jar >= jar_max; else capped_session if any earned_at of this session > at - cap_session_ms; else capped_hour if count(earned_at > at - 1 h) >= cap_per_hour; else capped_day if count(earned_at > at - 24 h) >= cap_per_day; else allow. Windows are half-open: an earn exactly one window ago no longer counts. Forgotten rows (earned_at 0) never count.

defaults.now: each event folds with now = its at (no clamping in these vectors)

model.per_event_expect: state of the vector's session after the event, 'earned' = a treat dropped by this event
model.final_expect: treats = treats earned in the vector; finished_seq = meta.finished_seq increments; open_turn = open turn key or null

transitions.session_start: state idle (an ended session restarts idle)
transitions.turn_start: a still-open turn closes neutrally (no treat, no finished_seq); open the new turn (tools 0, started at); state working
transitions.activity: (a) key == open turn: count a new distinct tool; waiting/idle -> working. (b) key == last done turn and at <= last_done_ms + late_tool_ms: count a new distinct tool toward the finished turn; if it earned nothing and was not re-checked, re-run the treat check once (duration = last_done_ms - its start). (c) key == last done turn, at > last_done_ms + late_tool_ms and a tool not seen in that turn: continuation - reopen the turn (same start, its tools + 1), state working. (d) otherwise only last_event_ms
transitions.waiting: state waiting (approval rows: their own row)
transitions.idle_prompt: state idle; the open turn stays open
transitions.turn_done: closes the open turn with the same key: state idle, finished_seq++ (interactive sessions only), treat check with tools = counted + payload tools. No matching open turn -> only last_event_ms
transitions.turn_failed: closes only the matching turn, no treat: state error, error_at_ms = at
transitions.turn_cancelled: closes only the matching turn, no treat: state idle. Keyless: closes the open turn only if it started before at
transitions.session_end: state ended; an open turn closes neutrally

model.approval_rows: Hermes approval_key events use a separate row keyed by HMAC(approval_key): waiting -> waiting; activity with the same key -> idle; nothing else touches it
model.non_interactive: tracked (state machine runs) but never counts for the face, never increments finished_seq and never earns
model.hello: the first non-test event of a client since Connect sets first_seen_ms and hello_seq++ (any interactivity); see fold_vectors

events.note: late tool of the finished turn
arrives in a later batch; at <= last_done + 1 s; re-check earns

fold.rule: outcomes in order: duplicate (dedupe_key exists: unlink, no row change) -> dropped_off (meta.enabled = 0) -> dropped_old (at < now - max_event_age_ms) -> clamp (at > now + future_clamp_ms -> at = now, still folded) -> dropped_child -> test (only test_state/test_at_ms) -> client record (+hello) -> no_life (stop) -> folded

order.when: life == null (first run, or after a goodbye/death)
a need is empty (now) or critical
a new test done, hello or finished_seq inside its window

priority.need_pick: among needs at the highest present group (now/critical first, then soon), pick by need_priority; the line uses that need's own level
priority.counting_app: an agent.apps entry whose stale_at_ms > now
priority.app_order: agent.apps order (since_ms ascending, then client order); {app} is the first app in the row's set, {app2} the second
priority.waiting_app: the waiting app with the latest since_ms (ties: client order)

celebrate.test: agent.test.state == 'done' and test.at_ms > seen.test_at_ms and now < at_ms + celebrate_window_ms
celebrate.hello: hello_seq > seen.hello_seq and now < hello_at_ms + celebrate_window_ms
celebrate.finished: finished_seq > seen.finished_seq and now >= finished_at_ms + celebrate_grace_ms and now < finished_at_ms + celebrate_window_ms and finished_app is not a counting working app

lines.finished: act.done_full if finished_jar_full, else act.done_treat if finished_treat, else act.done

celebrate.seen: the UI records the celebrated seq/at and passes it back as `seen`

priority.treats_visible: treats.jar > 0 and life awake (not care.sleeping) and not fainted and enabled
priority.star_badge: rows 7-9 show the star badge when treats_visible
priority.wake_at_ms: null when Off. Otherwise the minimum of these future times (null when none), whatever row wins: stale_at_ms of each counting app; for each unseen celebration candidate whose window is still open, its grace end if still ahead, else its window end; the error frame end and the oops end while ahead
priority.vars: exactly the placeholders of the line template; {app}/{app2} are client ids (the UI maps them to display names)
